filename: Constrained Earth system models show a stronger reduction in future Northern Hemisphere snowmelt water.pdf
title: Constrained Earth system models show a stronger reduction in future Northern Hemisphere snowmelt water
code_availability: Codes to reproduce the study are available via GitHub at https://github.com/alanchai/Overcoming-the-Northern-Hemisphere-snow-water-resources-paradox.git (ref. 80).
testbed_rationale: The study applies statistical emergent constraints to GCM/ESM multi-model ensemble projections and observation-based reanalyses. It does not provide high-resolution cloud-resolving or LES simulation benchmarks designed for machine learning parameterization training.
pain_points: Drizzle problem: GCMs frequently overestimate light snowfall frequency, causing severe positive biases in snow accumulation and SWE.
Glaciated grid cells in ESMs: Lack of distinction between glaciers and seasonal snow pack leads to unrealistic SWE accumulation (>500 kg m^-2) in mountain regions.
High observational uncertainty across historical SWE datasets due to sparse in situ networks, retrieval algorithm assumptions, and forcing inaccuracies.
extraction_notes: The paper uses statistical hierarchical emergent constraints rather than neural networks or standard machine learning models. Supported by NSF LEAP Science and Technology Center (grant no. 2019625, co-authored by Pierre Gentine).
